title: Minions & Monsters' Scares Up #1 Spot, But Franchise Faces Soft Opening
summary: The Minions have traded world domination for Hollywood dreams in 'Minions & Monsters,' which claimed the top spot at the North American box office on Friday with $16 million from 4,243 theaters. The animated sequel, set in the 1920s, follows the yellow henchmen as wannabe filmmakers hunting for real monsters to star in their creature feature. Through Sunday, it's expected to gross $39.5 million domestically, bringing its total since opening July 1 to a soft $64 million. For a franchise that has reliably minted money — 2015's 'Minions' earned $1.15 billion globally, and 2022's 'Minions: The Rise of Gru' hit $940 million — this opening is notably lower. However, overseas markets are picking up the slack, with an estimated $87 million by Sunday. The voice cast includes Pierre Coffin, Trey Parker, Allison Janney, and Jeff Bridges, with Coffin co-directing. Meanwhile, 'Toy Story 5' isn't going quietly. In its third weekend, the Pixar sequel added $13 million on Friday, pushing its North American total to about $367 million. It's on track to challenge 'Toy Story 4's $1 billion worldwide haul. Third place went to Angel Studio's 'Young Washington,' a Revolutionary War adventure starring William Franklyn-Miller as a young George Washington, which earned $7.4 million. The real drama was in fourth: DC's 'Supergirl' plummeted 76% from its disastrous $37.1 million opening, earning just $3.6 million on Friday. Analysts project a $200 million global finish, leaving the film about $100 million in the red. Steven Spielberg's 'Disclosure Day' rounded out the top five with $2.2 million. While 'Minions & Monsters' isn't breaking records, its family-friendly charm and international appeal should keep it afloat. After all, who can resist Minions with a movie camera?
why_it_matters: Box office trends reveal how audiences spend their time and money—shaping what studios will greenlight next. A soft opening for a megafranchise might signal that viewers are growing tired of the same characters, or that streaming is eating into theater attendance. Understanding this helps you see why certain movies get made and others don't.

background_read: The Minions are small, yellow henchmen who first appeared in the 2010 film 'Despicable Me.' Their slapstick humor and gibberish language turned them into a global phenomenon, spawning their own spin-off series. The 2015 'Minions' and 2022 'Minions: The Rise of Gru' each earned close to or over a billion dollars. They are famously tied to the 1960s/70s timeline of the main movies, so this 1920s prequel is a bold shift.

The animation industry has been dominated by sequels and established franchises for years because they seem like safe bets. But even giants like Pixar (behind 'Toy Story 5') and DC (with 'Supergirl') face risks—audiences are more selective, and a 'disastrous' opening can send a film straight to the 'red ink', meaning it loses tens of millions of dollars for the studio. Trey Parker (co-creator of South Park) and Allison Janney (Oscar-winning actress) bring star power to the Minions cast, alongside the longtime Minion voice Pierre Coffin.

perspectives.description: The Minions reliably entertain families, and the 1920s setting offers fresh slapstick possibilities. With a strong overseas start ($87 million), it could still become profitable. The voice cast adds comedic cachet, and as a summer release, it fills a need for lighthearted fare. For Universal, the brand remains a valuable asset.

perspectives.perspective: Negative / critical (franchise fatigue and box office realities)
perspectives.description: A $39.5 million opening weekend is modest for a series that once opened to $115 million. It suggests audiences may be tiring of prequels and spin-offs. Meanwhile, 'Supergirl' lost a fortune—a warning that not every superhero property works. Theaters need fresh ideas, not just recycled animation. If tentpoles underperform, studios might slash risky projects.

perspectives.perspective: Neutral / analytical (the economics of global releases)
perspectives.description: Hollywood now relies heavily on international markets; 60-70% of revenue often comes from abroad. So while domestic numbers seem soft, the overseas performance can mask or validate. The summer of 2025 has a crowded slate—sequels and originals are fighting for attention. Box office is a snapshot, but profitability includes streaming and merchandise too.

If the Minions franchise continues to see diminishing returns, Illumination Entertainment might push for a break or take creative risks—perhaps a spin-off with entirely new characters. The failure of 'Supergirl' could accelerate DC's shift away from solo character films. For viewers, the outcome might mean fewer sequels and more original stories in the future.
